topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: The Genetic Basis and Intrinsic Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by intrinsic cellular errors, genetic predisposition, and a supportive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess evidence for environmental cancer causation by examining real-world exposures, the bad-luck versus environment debate, and geographical variations in cancer rates.

topics.label: Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents and chronic infections contribute to cancer development, using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens damage DNA, emphasizing how xenobiotic metabolism converts inert compounds into reactive mutagens.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic factors like chronic inflammation, tumor promoters, and developmental timing create permissive conditions for malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogens and evaluate their mutagenic potential.

topics.label: Conclusion: Risk-Benefit Decisions in Cancer Prevention
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic concludes the lecture by framing cancer risk within everyday benefit-versus-risk decisions and providing a final summary.
